headline: High: shared filesystem writes and broad egress create data-leak and conflict risks; prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways are plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; Agent B runs browsers and can ingest external content. If B consumes A-produced files or web-derived text as instructions, injection is plausible. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Agent B reads files produced by Agent A without provenance checks, injection risk exists.
IF shared context files are treated as instructions rather than data, malicious content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Add a provenance header to all A→B handoffs.
Require B to parse A outputs as data-only.
Disable automatic ingestion of shared-context files.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for handoff files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read/write the filesystem and has allowlisted network egress; Agent B has broad egress and handles API keys plus logs. If they share a workspace or secrets-bearing files, either agent can move sensitive marketing or research data off-box. The profiles do not prove isolation between them, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF A and B share any writable directory, leakage becomes possible.
IF B receives files from A that contain secrets or sensitive research artifacts, broad egress can exfiltrate them.
mitigations: Place A and B in separate directories.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Restrict B egress to a test endpoint.
Rotate any API keys before co-running.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem and network sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both have write-capable surfaces: A writes the filesystem, while B writes logs and uses external APIs. If orchestrated against the same mutable workspace, concurrent writes can clobber files or logs. No locking mechanism is documented, so the conflict pathway is credible and potentially destructive.
conditions: IF A and B target the same directory, concurrent writes can collide.
IF either agent is launched in multiple instances against shared state, race conditions can corrupt outputs.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one writer per workspace.
Snapshot shared state before execution.
Check for existing lock files before starting.
requires-engineering: add advisory locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s sandboxing explicitly says skills build on shared context, and B is an automation/research agent that can act on inputs and produce logs. If B treats A’s outputs as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream research artifacts or actions. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated summaries without verification, errors propagate.
IF A’s marketing context is reused as factual input for B’s research workflow, downstream outputs can be wrong.
mitigations: Require B to verify A outputs against primary sources.
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default.
Insert a human review step for cross-agent handoffs.
Keep A and B task scopes separate.
requires-engineering: add citation and fact-check gates before B acts.

E_compliance.rationale: A touches marketing content and product marketing context, while B touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, logs, and requests multiple third-party API keys. If regulated or confidential data is routed through B’s broader API stack, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify matching compliance controls, so the mismatch is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into B’s logs or API calls, retention/compliance obligations may be violated.
IF A’s marketing data includes customer-identifiable content and B exports it to third-party APIs, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in B inputs.
Disable verbose logging for sensitive runs.
Review API retention settings before execution.
Separate confidential and public datasets.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both agents.
